metadata.title: Claude, Deal Tracker.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude's deal-tracker skill understands deals on its own or just executes a written spec, using the skill's own job description, steps, and trigger phrases as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that deal-tracker gives the same reliable output for exactly what's written in its steps, and nothing at all for what isn't.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the ACME Series C deal card: an overdue milestone gets flagged when the request matches a written step; the same card stays inert when asked something the six trigger phrases never cover)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude's deal tracker is a smart assistant that already knows their pipeline. It isn't — it's a scripted set of steps. So what does the deal-tracker skill actually do?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude, Deal Tracker. It's a SMART assistant that tracks my deals — so what does it actually do?', hesitates on 'smart', corrects to 'scripted', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude, Deal Tracker.
It's a SMART assistant
that tracks my deals —
so what does it actually do?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('smart' -> 'scripted') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. Deal-tracker's SKILL.md says exactly what to do: track live deals — milestones, deadlines, action items, status — and surface what's overdue. Plain instructions. No hidden reasoning.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon labelled deal-tracker/ with a SKILL.md card inside it; the job description typing out beside it

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'deal-tracker/' sits left, a card labelled 'SKILL.md' fixed inside it. To the right, four short labels type in one at a time: milestones, deadlines, action items, status. A thin arrow runs from the SKILL.md card to a note reading 'Claude reads, then acts.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order, one deal at a time. Take Acme — a live deal moving through the pipeline. When a milestone's deadline passes, deal-tracker flags it overdue. Exactly what step three says to do.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a deal card labelled ACME · Series C moving through numbered steps; on step three its milestone deadline passes and an OVERDUE flag lights up in terracotta

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one deal, moving through the steps
production_viz.mechanic: Three numbered step boxes sit left to right. A deal card labelled 'ACME · Series C' with a small milestone line 'Term sheet — due Fri' slides into step one, then step two, then step three. THE ANCHOR. On step three, the milestone's date crosses a small clock icon and an 'OVERDUE' flag lights up in terracotta beside the card. THIS EXACT CARD RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Now ask Acme's tracker something the spec never lists — draft the counterparty's redline. Nothing happens. No fallback, no guess. Same input, same reliable output for what's written; anything outside those six trigger phrases, it simply doesn't reach.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same ACME Series C card; a new request bubble reads draft the counterparty's redline; no step lights up, the card stays dim, no flag appears

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — outside the spec, nothing happens
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 CARD RETURNS, identical: 'ACME · Series C', the same three step boxes. A speech-bubble request types in above it: 'draft the counterparty's redline.' No step brightens, no flag appears — the whole row stays at resting dim. A line of small italic text appears beneath: 'no fallback. no guess.'

beats.narration_text: Deal-tracker gives the same reliable output for exactly what's written in its steps — and nothing at all for what isn't.

props.quote: Deal-tracker gives the same reliable output for exactly what's written in its steps — and nothing at all for what isn't.
props.sparkLine: Reliable inside the spec. Nothing outside it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Read the deal-tracker skill, then track three deals: Acme, a Series C with a milestone due Friday; Beta Corp, an add-on due next Tuesday; Gamma LLC, a refi with no deadline set. Ask for the pipeline view and anything overdue. Then ask something the skill never lists — like negotiating strategy — and watch: does it say that's outside the skill, or does it guess? Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Read the deal-tracker skill, then track three deals: Acme (Series C, milestone due Friday), Beta Corp (add-on, due next Tuesday), Gamma LLC (refi, no deadline set). Show the pipeline view and anything overdue.
